title: Password Storage and Authentication
subtitle: bcrypt, Argon2, and secure credential handling

content.text: Passwords must never be stored in plaintext or with fast hashes like SHA-256. Use purpose-built slow algorithms: bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2.

content.code:
from argon2 import PasswordHasher
from argon2.exceptions import VerifyMismatchError

ph = PasswordHasher(
    time_cost=3,       # number of iterations
    memory_cost=65536, # 64 MB
    parallelism=4
)

# Hash password at registration
hash = ph.hash("user_password_here")
print(hash)  # $argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=3,p=4$...

# Verify at login
try:
    ph.verify(hash, "user_password_here")
    print("Password valid")
except VerifyMismatchError:
    print("Wrong password")

content.definition: A random value added to the password before hashing to prevent precomputed rainbow table attacks.

content.text: Argon2id is the current recommended algorithm for password hashing (OWASP 2024). Bcrypt is a solid fallback.

questions.question: Why are bcrypt/Argon2 preferred over SHA-256 for passwords?
options: They are intentionally slow, making brute force impractical
questions.explanation: Password hashing algorithms like Argon2 are deliberately slow and memory-intensive to make offline brute-force attacks impractical.

faq.q: Should I add my own salt?
faq.a: No. Argon2 and bcrypt include automatic salt generation. Adding your own on top provides no benefit and may introduce bugs.
